thread:
maria: :rotating_light: CS escalation - multiple customers reporting intermittent 5xx + long streaming timeouts hitting hosted inference endpoint /v1/generate since ~09:50 UTC. Reports show 503 and connection resets. Example request-id: req_8f3ab2. Any oncall?

nina-oncall: I'm on it. Joining traces now. Can someone paste a sample curl or request payload from the customer?

anya-cs: Here's the payload (redacted): `{"model":"redwood-v2-small","prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}`. Customer noted it started after a spike of concurrent long-streaming calls. They saw p95 token latency jump and client SDKs show socket timeouts ~30s.

raj: I'll check gateway logs and ingress pools. Noted a recent routing rule change to add stricter rate caps for free-tier about 08:30 UTC. Could be related.

maria: Customer also reported that retries momentarily drop error ratio but then returns. They have bursty fanout.

nina-oncall: Looking at apigw -> inference-proxy traces: a lot of 502/503 from sidecar where the backend returned 504s. Suspect backend queueing/backpressure. Attaching sample log snippet: ```[2024-11-02T09:57:12Z] req=req_8f3ab2 upstream_status=504 backend_queue_depth=27 conn_time_ms=3120```

sam: backend_queue_depth 27 is high. Which pool?

raj: EU-west pool node set A. There was an autoscaler event that failed to scale up due to instance init timeouts ~08:50 UTC (kube events show image pull throttling on two nodes).

nina-oncall: That would cause queueing + aggressive ratecap to trip, leading to 503s at the gateway. Are we seeing circuit-breaker kicks?

ops-bot: circuit-breaker:hosted-inference-eu-west poolA status -> OPEN (since 1769009958) fallback_route -> enabled.

maria: Customer-facing short mitigation? Can we toggle fallback_route to cheaper model or increase burst capacity?

raj: I can temporarily disable the strict ratecap config for poolA and increase per-client burst allowance. Will do a controlled change.

sam: Also recommend enabling soft-fallback to redwood-v1-small for streaming requests for latency-sensitive customers. That avoids long KV/cache warmups.

nina-oncall: Making the ratecap change now. Patch: `kubectl apply -f ratecap-patch.yaml --namespace hosted-inference` (rolling update). I'll monitor errors after patch.

maria: :thumbsup: please confirm when stable and we can tell CS to update customers.

(4 minutes pass)

ops-bot: deploy:ratecap-patch succeeded on poolA. New config active at 1769010050.

nina-oncall: Error rate dropped to baseline within ~60s after patch. p95 token latency down from 18s -> 2.1s for impacted customers. Observed reduction in 503s.

anya-cs: Sharing to customers: "We've applied a temporary routing and ratecap change to reduce 503s; our engineers are investigating root cause and will follow up with action items."

maria: Great. Next: RCA checklist + action items. Preliminary cause hypothesis: autoscale cold-start + image pull throttling -> backend capacity lag -> queueing -> circuit-breaker + strict ratecaps -> 503s and streaming timeouts.

raj: Evidence list:
- kube events: multiple `ImagePullBackOff` 08:47-08:55 UTC on poolA nodes
- backend logs: `backend_queue_depth` spikes 08:50-09:00 UTC
- deploy logs: no config deploys in the window, but cloud provider reported transient OSS rate limits on image registry

sam: Action items (short-term):
1) Add temporary pre-warmed instances in EU-west pool during peak hours (ops runbook).
2) Relax strict free-tier ratecap fallback for bursty streaming to allow short bursts for existing customers. (raj)
3) Add health-check gating so autoscaler doesn't mark node ready until sidecar image fully pulled. (infra)

maria: Action items (long-term):
1) Implement async queue backpressure metrics (expose queue depth per-pool per-tenant). (platform)
2) Improve image pull resiliency (registry mirrors, cached images on node). (eng-infra)
3) Update fallback policy to prefer lower-latency smaller models for streaming when primary model latency > threshold. (runtime)

nina-oncall: I'll create a quick postmortem doc and assign owners. Also recommend contacting cloud provider to understand the registry limits and request higher quota or mirror.

anya-cs: For comms: I'll send an interim note to affected customers summarizing mitigation and ETA for full RCA.

maria: Owners: raj (short-term ratecap + scaling), sam (fallback policy), nina-oncall (postmortem + monitoring), eng-infra (image pull resilience). Please add estimated ETA for each item in the postmortem doc.

raj: Will follow up with short-term patch timeline: relaxing ratecap completed; pre-warm plan drafted, ETA tomorrow EOD.

sam: I'll prototype fallback policy change in a canary and test on a small set of customers this week.

ops-bot: incident-status: mitigated -> partial (customer impact reduced). followup-doc -> https://redwood.internal/pm/1769009999

maria: Thanks team. Postmortem follow-up: include specific repro steps, the customer request-id, and dashboards (p95 token latency, queue depth, image-pull errors) so CS can reference.

nina-oncall: Noting timeline for postmortem: draft in 24 hours, final in 72 hours. Assigning owners in doc.

anya-cs: I'll prepare customer-facing language once we have RCA draft.

maria: Closing war-room. If anything regresses, ping this thread or @nina-oncall. :white_check_mark:
